screening_results.reason: This study reports voxelwise FDG-PET analyses using SPM96 in a clinically defined FTD sample (Lund and Manchester criteria) and compares the FTD group (n=10) to healthy controls (n=46) at whole-brain voxel level in stereotaxic space. Imaging modality matches FDG-PET (I3). The patient sample includes clinically diagnosed FTD with behavioral features meeting Lund & Manchester criteria (consistent with bvFTD; I4). Sample sizes meet minimums (FTD n=10, controls n=46) (I5). Between-group voxelwise contrasts (FTD vs HS) were performed in standard stereotaxic space (SPM normalization) and reported as whole-brain results (I6, I7). Results are reported in text with voxelwise/statistical maps and Brodmann areas (acceptable reporting formats) (I8). No exclusion criteria were met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Note: diagnosis is reported as FTD per Lund & Manchester criteria rather than explicitly labeled “bvFTD” in the text, but behavioral criteria were required for inclusion, so it is appropriate to include.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for bvFTD VBM studies. It used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses (MNI-based normalization and atlas localization) with clearly described between-group contrasts (FTD vs controls) that are not pooled with other patient groups (I6, I7, I8). The FTD group comprises 8 clinically diagnosed patients (Neary criteria, consistent with behavioral-variant FTD) and there are 20 healthy controls, satisfying sample-size requirements (I4, I5). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, no disqualifying comorbid sample, not non-empirical, not a connectivity/DTI/thickness-only paper). Therefore I include this study for the meta-analysis focused on bvFTD VBM findings.

The study uses task-based fMRI (n-back) and includes 7 FTD patients, and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group results with Talairach coordinates (supplementary tables). However, it does not explicitly state that the patient sample is behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease (I4 not clearly met). Also, the between-group contrasts reported compare FTD to Alzheimer’s disease patients rather than to healthy controls; inclusion criterion I6 requires a between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls. Therefore not all required inclusion criteria are satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study reports voxelwise FDG-PET analyses in a sample of 29 clinically diagnosed FTD patients (PPA and semantic dementia explicitly excluded), with age-matched controls. The methods use SPM in MNI space and report group-level, whole-brain results (conjunction and subtraction analyses) including MNI coordinates (e.g., 4,62,-6; Z=7.03). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (29 patients; controls per center ≥6). The analyses are whole-brain voxelwise (not ROI-only) and the bvFTD-like clinical phenotype (behavioral/social disinhibition, loss of insight) is consistent with behavioral-variant FTD. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review/meta-analysis, ROI-only, seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness only) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review objective.

Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM as imaging modality), I5 (FTD patient group n=29 and control group n=12, both ≥6), I7 (reports whole-brain, voxelwise VBM group-level results in Talairach space). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (paper does not explicitly state inclusion of clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD/bvFTD or Pick’s disease; FTD sample is described as heterogeneous subgroups including primary progressive aphasia and a subgroup with “disorder of social and executive functioning,” but bvFTD is not explicitly identified), I6 (no between-group contrast reported specifically for a bvFTD-only group versus controls; results are reported for the pooled FTD group). No exclusion criteria from the review (E5–E9) are triggered. Because the review targets bvFTD-specific whole-brain contrasts, lack of an isolated bvFTD group/contrast prevents inclusion.

This is an empirical VBM study (SPM99 voxelwise analyses) reporting whole-brain, group-level contrasts in Talairach space. The sample includes clinically diagnosed FTD subgroups, including a NON-APH subgroup described as having social/behavioral and executive impairment (behavioral-variant–type presentation) with n=14. Imaging/control group sizes meet the >=6 threshold (NON-APH n=14; imaging controls n=12). The paper reports subgroup VBM results (FTD subgroups vs healthy seniors) with coordinates and figures/tables (Table 4, Fig.2) so bvFTD-relevant whole-brain contrasts are provided and not pooled with other diagnoses. Full text contains methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7,I8 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical study of FTD with adequate sample sizes and includes clinically diagnosed frontal-variant FTD (bvFTD-like) participants, but it does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET. The imaging approach is manual volumetric ROI-based MRI and the paper reports region-of-interest volumetric comparisons rather than any whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results or stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) coordinates. Therefore it fails the modality and whole-brain/coordinate reporting requirements for the meta-analysis and meets the exclusion for ROI-only studies.

The study is excluded because it does not specifically report results for clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease patients (I4 not met). Although whole-brain, voxelwise contrasts comparing the FTD group to controls are reported with stereotactic coordinates, the patient sample is described generically as FTD and not explicitly as bvFTD; therefore the requirement that results come from a bvFTD target group (I6 and I7) is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This study reports 18F-FDG PET voxelwise (SPM99) comparisons between a clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia (FTD) group (n=25) and healthy controls (n=15). The FTD group was diagnosed per revised Lund-Manchester criteria, with clinical features and selection (exclusion of primary progressive aphasia) consistent with the behavioral variant presentation. Imaging modality (FDG-PET), sample sizes, and independent group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with Talairach coordinates are provided for the FTD vs control contrast (FTD not pooled with SD). No exclusion criteria are met. Caveat: the paper uses the term “FTD” rather than explicitly “bvFTD,” but the clinical description, diagnostic criteria, and exclusion of PPA indicate the sample corresponds to behavioral-variant FTD. Therefore it meets required inclusion criteria for the review.

The study is excluded because it does not provide bvFTD-specific whole-brain voxelwise results. Met: I3 (FDG‑PET used) and I5 (patient group N=14 ≥6). Not met: I4 — although the sample includes FTD cases within a pooled FTLD group, the paper does not report results for clinically-diagnosed bvFTD (behavioral variant) separately; I6 — no between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD-only group to controls (or EOAD) without pooling with other FTLD subgroups; I7 — no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD-only target group. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical VBM study that compares a clinically defined frontotemporal dementia (FTD) patient group (behaviorally defined FTD; patients with predominant behavioral/frontal syndrome, excluding progressive aphasia/semantic dementia) to healthy controls using whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses. Imaging modality is VBM (I3). The patient sample includes 9 FTD participants and 26 controls, meeting the minimum N≥6 for both groups (I5). Between-group voxelwise contrasts are reported in stereotactic space (SPM coordinates; e.g., periaqueductal gray at (0,-28,-10)) and whole-brain group-level voxelwise results are presented and attributed to the FTD sample (I6, I7). Results are reported as corrected and uncorrected voxelwise findings and coordinates (I8). No exclusion criteria (reviews-only, ROI-only, non-empirical, DTI/FC/CTh-only, or prohibited comorbid-sample) are met. Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion).

This study examines frontal-variant FTLD (fv-FTLD), equivalent to behavioral variant FTD, using 18FDG-PET (and [11C]MDL PET) with voxelwise SPM analyses. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (sb: whole fv-FTLD vs controls; apathetic vs controls; disinhibited vs controls; direct between-group contrasts) with coordinates in MNI space and cluster-level information. Patient group (n=18) and control group (n=24) meet sample-size thresholds; PET subgroup analyses included 8 patients and 6 controls (>=6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, no comorbid psychiatric/other dementia in sample, empirical FDG-PET whole-brain results reported). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This VBM study includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients (including frontal-variant/bvFTD cases) and meets sample-size requirements, but it does not report a bvFTD-specific between-group whole-brain contrast versus controls. Whole-brain VBM results are reported for a heterogeneous FTD group pooled across subtypes rather than for a distinct bvFTD group that is not pooled with other patient groups. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria requiring (I6) a between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD group (not pooled) to controls and (I7) at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the target (bvFTD) sample. No exclusion criteria from the provided list were triggered and the full text appears complete.

This is an empirical 18F-FDG PET study using voxel-wise SPM analysis (whole-brain) comparing 29 clinically diagnosed FTD patients to 11 healthy controls. The sample (n=29) meets the minimum size, and the authors explicitly excluded language variants (progressive nonfluent aphasia, semantic dementia), indicating the sample represents behavioral/clinical FTD cases. Analyses were performed in stereotactic space (normalized to MNI and coordinates converted to Talairach) and report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates (Table 3 and figures). All required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, no disallowed modalities). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

The study reports whole-brain, voxelwise FDG-PET SPM analyses comparing FTD groups to controls and has adequate sample sizes (FTD n=29; controls n=11; FTD/MND n=8). However, the paper does not explicitly state that the patient sample consists of clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease. The diagnostic label used is the consensus clinical diagnostic criteria for FTD (Neary et al.), but subtype breakdown (bvFTD vs other FTD variants) is not provided for the main FTD group. Inclusion criterion I4 (explicit bvFTD or Pick's disease sample) is therefore not met, and I6 (a between-group contrast explicitly of bvFTD versus controls) cannot be confirmed. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I7, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I6. No exclusion criteria from the provided list are triggered.

This study reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) whole-brain analyses comparing pathologically defined FTD subgroups (including Pick disease) to healthy controls, with MRI data normalized to the Montreal Neurologic Institute (MNI) template. The sample includes 21 FTD patients (subgroups: FTD-U, PiD, tau exon 10+16) and 20 controls (each group ≥6). VBM results are reported as group-level, voxelwise contrasts versus controls and displayed in figures/tables (whole-brain voxelwise results, with MNI normalization). Because the inclusion criteria allow Pick disease patients as target samples and require VBM and whole-brain voxelwise contrasts, all required inclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

Although it is an empirical study of clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia with a sufficient patient sample (I4 and I5 met: 29 FTD patients diagnosed by consensus criteria), imaging was limited to visual/region-based assessment of SPECT/PET laterality and quadrant predominance without voxelwise coordinate results or explicit FDG-PET specification (I3 not satisfied/uncertain). Full text appears incomplete for purposes of meta-analysis (no coordinates, no voxelwise methods/tables provided); fulltext_incomplete=true. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5. While this study uses FDG-PET (I3), includes clinically diagnosed frontal-variant FTD patients (equivalent to bvFTD; I4), has sufficient patient sample size (n=70; I5), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise component images in MNI space (I7, acceptable reporting format I8), it does not present a between-group voxelwise contrast comparing the bvFTD/fv-FTD group directly to healthy controls in MNI or Talairach space (criterion I6). The paper focuses on within-group PCA decomposition of patient scans rather than reporting a between-group coordinate-based contrast vs controls; therefore it fails to meet inclusion criterion I6 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study meets the review criteria: it used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and performed whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons registered to MNI space (I6, I7). The sample comprises pathologically-confirmed FTLD-U (n=11) and FTLD-MND (n=7) cases who “fulfilled consensus criteria for frontotemporal dementia” and are described as having a frontal variant clinical presentation, which corresponds to behavioral/ frontal-variant FTD (bvFTD) for the purposes of the review (I4). Patient group sizes meet the minimum (≥6) and controls are n=18 (I5). Whole-brain results are reported in the text and figures (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (no review/meta-analysis, ROI-only, non-empirical, seed-FC/DTI/thickness-only methods, or psychiatric comorbidity reported). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion so is complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical, longitudinal FDG-PET study of ‘frontal variant’ FTD (behavioral variant phenotype). It used whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses and reports between-group contrasts with Talairach coordinates comparing 22 clinically diagnosed FTD patients to 15 healthy controls. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). Whole-brain results for the target (FTD) group are clearly reported (baseline and follow-up) and coordinates/cluster maxima are provided. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the bvFTD meta-analysis.

Although this empirical paper uses VBM (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed frontal variant FTD subgroup (behavioral variant FTLD/FTD) with n=14 and a control group with n=20 (I4, I5 satisfied), it does not report a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise between-group contrast in MNI/Talairach space that isolates the bvFTD (FTD) group versus controls. The VBM analyses reported are correlational (brain volume correlated with antisaccade performance) and, importantly, the primary VBM models controlled for or used a combined FTLD group (FTD+SD+PA) rather than presenting a direct bvFTD (FTD) >/< control voxelwise contrast. Therefore the study fails to meet I6 and I7 (no bvFTD-specific whole-brain between-group voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7. Exclusion criteria met: none.

This VBM study includes a behavioral-variant FTD (FTD) subgroup (n=30) and reports whole-brain voxelwise VBM results, but it does NOT present a between-group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD (FTD) to healthy controls in stereotactic space. Controls were explicitly not used in the VBM regressions, and the main findings are across a mixed patient sample (correlations with empathy) or subgroup-by-covariate interactions rather than a direct bvFTD vs. control group contrast with MNI/Talairach coordinates. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (no between-group contrast of bvFTD vs controls). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (bvFTD/FTD patients included), I5 (adequate sample sizes for patient and control groups), I7 (reports whole-brain voxelwise results identified for the FTD subgroup via covariate interaction). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no direct between-group contrast of bvFTD vs controls reported). No exclusion criteria from the list were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria: imaging modality is FDG-PET (I3); the sample comprises clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia patients per Lund–Manchester criteria with other FTLD variants (semantic dementia, non-fluent progressive aphasia) excluded, consistent with a behavioral-variant FTD sample (I4) — diagnosis based on clinical criteria and PET pattern; sample sizes meet minimums (29 patients, 16 controls) (I5); the paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing FTD to controls with coordinates reported in Talairach/MNI space (I6); whole-brain, voxelwise group-level SPM results are clearly identified as coming from the patient group (I7); results are reported as coordinates/figures and described in text (I8). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria were met.

This VBM study of frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD) meets several inclusion criteria: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients with early prominent behavioural features consistent with bvFTD within the sample), I5 (≥6 patients and ≥6 controls), and I8 (reports whole-brain results in tables/figures). However it does NOT meet key meta-analysis requirements: I6 and I7 are not satisfied because the paper does not report a between-group whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD (behavioral-variant FTD) group to healthy controls — instead analyses are performed on the mixed FTLD cohort (13 FTD + 3 SD) or on behavioural covariates within that pooled group. Therefore the target sample (bvFTD) is not isolated for a between-group voxelwise contrast, so the study cannot be included. Exclusion criteria met: none ([]) .

Although this study uses VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (I4), and has adequate group sizes (PGRN+ n=8, PGRN- n=8, controls) meeting the >=6 requirement (I5), it does NOT report a between-group whole-brain contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD-only group to controls (I6). The reported whole-brain VBM results are for genetic/pathological groups (PGRN+ and PGRN-) that include mixed clinical syndromes (bvFTD, SD, CBS), so the paper does not provide a group-level, whole-brain result clearly identified as coming solely from the target bvFTD sample (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Therefore the study is excluded for failing to meet I6 and I7. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3, I4, I5. Inclusion IDs not met: I6, I7.

Full text is complete and the study is empirical, uses FDG-PET and includes clinically diagnosed frontal variant/bvFTD patients (n=13) and controls (n=21). It reports whole-brain voxelwise SPM results correlating autobiographical memory measures with resting FDG uptake in the fv-FTD group (i.e., group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results in stereotactic space). However, the paper does not present a between-group voxelwise contrast (bvFTD patients versus controls) reported in MNI/Talairach coordinates. Inclusion criterion I6 (at least one between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls in defined stereotactic space) is not met, so the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply.

Patient sample size (n=17 total; 7 with stereotypies, 10 without) and control group (matched, n≈17) both exceed the minimum of 6. The paper provides whole-brain group-level results (FTLD vs controls and direct FTLD subgroup comparisons) and details preprocessing in MNI space. Instead, participants are classified by pathological subtype (FTLD‐T and FTLD‐U) and while the majority “presented clinically as frontotemporal dementia,” the paper does not clearly define or isolate a bvFTD clinical group nor report between-group voxelwise contrasts specifically for a bvFTD group versus controls. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I5 (patient groups have ≥6 participants; controls n=61), I8 (whole-brain results presented in figures/tables). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (does not specify clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick’s disease group), I6 (no between-group contrast reported specifically comparing a bvFTD group to controls in standardized stereotactic space), I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise result identified as coming from a bvFTD target sample). No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

While the study uses FDG-PET (meets I3), includes a patient group with Pick's disease / FTD and sufficient sample sizes (FTD n=14, controls n=33; meets I4 and I5), it does NOT report any group-level whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing bvFTD (or Pick's) to controls. The results are presented as diagnostic/visual assessments, region rating frequencies, and SSP individual-level statistical maps, but no whole-brain, group-level coordinate tables or voxelwise contrasts from the target patient group are provided. Therefore the study fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 and does not provide the necessary voxelwise whole-brain results. This places it within exclusion criterion E6 (no whole-brain results; only regional/visual/individual analyses).

This study reports FDG-PET (I3) on a clinically diagnosed frontal/behavioral variant FTD sample (bvFTD; I4). Imaging results are voxelwise SPM whole-brain analyses reported with Talairach coordinates and cluster statistics comparing patient groups to healthy controls (satisfies I6, I7, I8). PET subgroup sizes meet the minimum (H1 N=31, H2 N=10, controls N=16), and whole-brain between-group contrasts (H1 vs controls, H2 vs controls, and H1 vs H2) are reported, with coordinates provided. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the review.

This is an empirical VBM study that reports voxelwise group contrasts with coordinates comparing FTD patients to controls. Imaging modality: VBM (meets I3). Sample: includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients meeting Neary criteria and behavioral descriptions consistent with behavioral-variant FTD (meets I4). Sample sizes exceed thresholds (32 patients total, 27 with usable MRI; 47 controls) satisfying I5. The paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts (overeating FTD subgroup vs nonovereaters and controls) with stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach reported), satisfying I6 and I8. VBM analyses are voxelwise/group-level whole-brain comparisons within an a priori ROI and results are clearly identified as coming from the target patient group (meets I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only without voxelwise results, not only FC/DTI/thickness, and no disqualifying comorbid sample issues). Note: the authors use the term “FTD” and Neary criteria rather than explicitly ‘bvFTD’; behavioral descriptions and diagnostic criteria indicate behavioral-variant FTD, which slightly reduces but does not preclude inclusion. Overall confidence 0.85.

This FDG-PET study includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients and meets imaging modality (I3), includes FTD (behavioral syndrome) patients (I4), and has sufficient patient numbers (I5). However, it does not report a between-group contrast comparing bvFTD (or FTD) to healthy controls: the main voxelwise comparisons are FTLD+UIC vs FTLD−UIC, and subgroup analyses restricted to FTD compare incontinent vs continent FTD patients (no healthy control group). Inclusion criteria I6 (bvFTD vs controls contrast) and I7 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise result originating from a bvFTD vs control contrast) are not met. The FTD-restricted results did not survive correction and are reported only uncorrected, and the primary analyses pooled FTLD subtypes. Therefore it does not satisfy the review’s requirement for bvFTD vs control whole-brain contrasts. Full text appears complete.

This is a longitudinal, empirical study that used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (SPM2 optimized/modulated VBM) to compare MSTD (Tau +3 intron 10 mutation) patients to age- and gender-matched controls. The VBM analysis included 7 early-stage MSTD patients (all clinically diagnosed with bvFTD) and 19 controls, meeting the sample-size requirement. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts with significant clusters and refers to stereotactic locations in supplementary Table 4 (i.e., coordinates in a defined stereotactic space). Whole-brain voxelwise results are clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD-target sample. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, review/meta-analysis, methods-only, or disallowed imaging modalities) are met.

Because inclusion criterion I4 requires specifically clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick’s disease, this criterion is not met.
