No exclusion criteria from the review (E5–E9) appear to be met. Therefore the study must be excluded for not explicitly studying bvFTD/Pick’s disease.

This empirical study uses FDG-PET (I3) in a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (I4). The final patient group included 21 bvFTD patients and controls (≥6 each; I5). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain SPM analyses in standard MNI space with group comparisons (bvFTD vs controls) and regression analyses within the bvFTD group, with coordinates and FWE-corrected results (I6, I7). Results and coordinates are described in the text and figures/supplementary material (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: this is not a review/meta-analysis (not E5), it includes whole-brain results rather than ROI-only analyses (not E6), there is no indication of disqualifying psychiatric comorbidity or substance abuse in the bvFTD sample (E7 not met), it is empirical primary data (not E8), and it does not report only FC, DTI, or cortical thickness (not E9). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study should be excluded because it reports Freesurfer ROI-based structural volume analyses rather than VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET, and it does not present whole-brain voxelwise (MNI/Talairach) group-level results. Exclusion criterion met: E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients) and I5 (bvFTD group n=48 and controls n=94, both ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group contrasts reported in defined stereotactic space), and I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Given these mismatches with required imaging and whole-brain reporting, the study does not qualify for inclusion in this meta-analysis.

Excluded because study does not meet key inclusion criteria for a bvFTD-focused voxelwise meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET used), I5 (patient group n=14 ≥6; control comparator n=33). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (participants are described as pathologically confirmed FTLD but not specified as clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD or Pick's disease), I6 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results or coordinate tables provided). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (study reports regional visual/ROI-based assessments of predefined cortical regions rather than whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is ineligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis focused on bvFTD voxelwise whole-brain results.

Although this paper uses voxel-based morphometry (meets I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within the cohort (meets I4), it does NOT report whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts specifically for a clinically defined bvFTD group compared to controls in standard space (MNI/Talairach). The VBM results are reported for FTLD-TDP pathologic subtypes (type 1, 2, 3) rather than for a bvFTD diagnostic group, and there is no clear between-group contrast (bvFTD vs controls) presented. The bvFTD subgroup size and coordinate-based results for bvFTD are not provided, so inclusion criteria I5 (≥6 patients in the target patient group), I6 (between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls), and I7 (a whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD target sample) are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria from the review (E5–E9) clearly apply. Full text appears complete. Consequently the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

Although the study uses VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients among its sample (I4), has adequate sample sizes (42 patients, 30 controls; I5), and reports whole-brain VBM results for pathologic groups (so reporting format is acceptable, I8), it does NOT report a between-group contrast that directly compares a clinically defined bvFTD group to controls (in MNI/Talairach space) where the bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups (I6). Likewise, it does not provide a whole-brain group-level voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD target sample (I7). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to meet I6 and I7.

The study used VBM (I3), included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (fvFTLD subgroup; I4), and had sufficient sample sizes (19 bvFTD, 22 controls; I5). However, it does not report any between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing the bvFTD (fvFTLD) group directly to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space (I6 not met), nor does it present at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD subgroup (I7 not met). The reported VBM results are regression associations in the combined FTLD group; subgroup analyses for fvFTLD produced no significant whole-brain or SVC results. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply.

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=12) and controls (n=21), meeting I3, I4 and the sample-size criterion I5. However, the VBM analyses reported are correlational (gray-matter correlations with conjunction-search accuracy) across the pooled sample and an ANOVA on extracted voxel values; the paper does not present a whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrast (bvFTD vs. controls) reported in MNI/Talairach space or coordinate tables that unambiguously reflect bvFTD-specific, group-level voxelwise results. Therefore it fails I6 and I7 (no clearly reported whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD to controls). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met, the study is excluded.

This study does not meet the review’s target-sample and whole-brain contrast requirements. It includes FTLD patients (N=31) and uses 18F-FDG PET (I3 satisfied) and has sufficient patient sample size (I5 satisfied). However, it does not specify that the FTLD sample is clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease (I4 not met: FTLD is reported generally without bvFTD/Pick’s subgroup breakdown). The paper also does not report any between-group voxelwise contrast in stereotaxic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing a bvFTD group to controls (I6 not met) and therefore provides no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD target sample (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria from the list (E5–E9) are triggered. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and several are not, the study must be excluded.

This study performs voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses on a bvFTD subgroup (N=12) with comparison to healthy controls (12 for VBM; NC behavioral group N=16), reports whole-brain, voxelwise two-sample t-test contrasts and regression analyses relating IRI empathy scores to gray-matter atrophy using standardized coordinate space (SPM normalization to template), and presents voxelwise results (clusters reported and tabulated). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, no excluded imaging modality, sample excludes other dementia causes). Full text contains methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied.

This study uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry and includes a behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD) subgroup (n=10) and healthy controls (n=20). It reports group-level, whole-brain VBM correlational results for the combined FTLD group and for syndromic subgroups. However, it does not present a between-group voxelwise contrast of the bvFTD group versus healthy controls in stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) that isolates bvFTD (results are primarily correlational within groups and a combined FTLD vs control atrophy map is reported). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (no between-group contrast of bvFTD vs controls in defined stereotactic space). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This study uses VBM and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (16 bvFTD within 26 FTLD patients) and 21 healthy controls, and the patient and control sample sizes meet minimum thresholds. However the imaging analyses reported are voxelwise regression associations between grey matter and emotion-recognition performance within a combined FTLD cohort (and VBM was performed on FTLD patients only). The paper does not report a between-group voxelwise contrast comparing the bvFTD group (not pooled with other patient groups) to controls in standard stereotactic space, nor does it present bvFTD-specific whole-brain voxelwise results. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 required by the review. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an ROI-based structural MRI and postmortem study of bvFTD; it does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met), and it does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise results or stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) coordinates from between-group contrasts (I6 and I7 not met). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample) and I5 (>=6 patients and >=6 controls). Full text appears complete. Accordingly the study is excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the review. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses FDG-PET) and I5 (patient and control group sizes ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 — patients are described as FTLD (frontotemporal lobar degeneration) without specification that they are clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease; I6 — the paper does not report at least one between-group contrast in MNI/Talairach space comparing a bvFTD group to controls (no bvFTD-specific coordinate-based contrasts provided); I7 — it does not provide a clear group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result identified as coming from a bvFTD sample (results are SVM weight maps and ROI-based analyses rather than coordinate-based voxelwise contrasts for bvFTD). Exclusion criteria met: none applicable. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study is a retrospective case series of 8 patients with a clinical diagnosis of FTD and imaging evidence of brain sagging. It meets I3 (FDG-PET/SPECT was performed in 5 patients), I4 (patients were clinically diagnosed with FTD/bvFTD), and I5 (patient group N=8 ≥6). However it does NOT meet I6 (no between-group contrast vs. controls in MNI/Talairach space), and does NOT meet I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical results reported/coordinates provided). No exclusion criteria from the review are triggered. Therefore the paper must be excluded because it lacks the required between-group, whole-brain voxelwise comparisons/coordinates required by I6 and I7.

The study is excluded because it does not meet the sample size inclusion criterion I5. Although the paper uses VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD/PiD subjects (I4), reports between-group voxelwise contrasts with peak coordinates (I6), provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (I7), and reports results in tables/figures (I8), each of the reported patient subgroup contrasts (PiD n=5, CBD n=5, FTLD-TDP type 1 n=5) contains fewer than the required 6 patients, so I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore EXCLUDED due to failure to satisfy I5.

Although the study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and included a clinically-diagnosed FTD group (behavioral FTD features) with >=6 patients and adequate controls, it does NOT report any between-group, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrasts comparing the bvFTD/FTD group to controls. VBM results are presented as correlations across pooled subjects (patients and controls) and subgroup sizes for imaging analyses are mixed (FTD n=6 in MRI subset). Key inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (a bvFTD vs control whole-brain group contrast in stereotactic space) are not met, so the study cannot be included in the meta-analysis.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E6 — the study reports lobar/ROI volumetry (temporal and frontal lobe volumes and ratios) and does not present whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinate tables. 
(b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 — uses automated voxel-based volumetry (SPM5-based voxel approach akin to VBM); I4 — includes a bvFTLD subgroup (6 bvFTLD patients); I5 — sample sizes meet thresholds (bvFTLD n=6; controls n=30). 
(c) Inclusion criteria not met: I6 — no report of at least one between-group voxelwise contrast in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing the bvFTLD group to controls unpooled; I7 — no group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) result clearly identified for the target group. 
Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusion). Therefore the study is excluded because it provides only ROI/lobar volumetry without whole-brain voxelwise contrasts required by the review.

This is an empirical, whole-brain VBM study of behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD). It uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=14) (I4) with healthy controls (n=18) and an AD group (n=15) meeting the sample size threshold (I5). The paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts and covariate analyses in MNI space (methods state MNI registration) comparing bvFTD to controls/AD (I6), and provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (VBM and TBSS) clearly attributed to the bvFTD group (I7). Results are presented in tables/figures (including supplementary tables/figures and cluster coordinates) (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, no pooling of bvFTD with other disorders for the reported contrasts). Full text appears complete. Based on these points, the study meets all inclusion criteria and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an open-label FDG-PET study in FTD that includes a bvFTD subgroup (n=7) and reports voxelwise, group-level PET results (before vs after memantine) with coordinates. However, it does not include any between-group contrasts comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space. The meta-analysis requires at least one between-group contrast of bvFTD versus controls (I6). Therefore the study fails to meet inclusion criterion I6 and must be excluded.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. It uses resting-state fMRI and voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3). It includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient group (n=21) and matched controls (n=21) (I4,I5). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise between-group contrasts for functional connectivity (seed-based and ICA-derived networks) with results assessed in MNI space and cluster-level correction (I6,I7). Results are presented as voxelwise maps/figures and described in the text (I8). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met. Inclusion supports extraction of whole-brain voxelwise findings for bvFTD vs controls.

Full text is complete. The study uses whole-brain Voxel-Based Morphometry (SPM5) and reports voxelwise, group-level contrasts with coordinate results, and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD and Pick’s disease patient groups. However, both bvFTD patient groups have N=5 each, below the required minimum of 6 participants per patient group (I5 not met). All other applicable inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3, I4, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded solely due to insufficient patient group sample size.

Although this study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and includes a large cohort with clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD (bvFTD) and Pick’s disease cases, the voxelwise, whole-brain VBM results reported are organized by pathological groups (e.g., TDP-C, Pick’s, MAPT mutations, etc.), not by the clinical bvFTD syndromic group. The review inclusion requires at least one group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrast in standard space comparing a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (not pooled with other patient groups) to healthy controls. This study does not present such bvFTD-vs-control voxelwise coordinates or maps (MNI/Talairach) for the clinical bvFTD group, so it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7. Full text appears complete.

The full text reports whole-brain voxelwise VBM analyses (grey matter density maps, SPM5) and regression analyses mapped to MNI space, satisfying imaging modality requirements. The sample includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=14) and healthy controls (imaging contrasts vs. controls), meeting sample requirements (≥6 participants per group). The paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts for bvFTD versus controls (separate from other patient groups) and whole-brain results described in the text/figures/tables. No exclusion criteria are violated (not a review; not ROI-only; empirical VBM study; no disallowed modalities). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, imaging methods, results and discussion and appears complete for screening purposes.

The study used 18F-FDG PET imaging (I3) and included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=31) meeting the minimum sample-size criterion (I4, I5). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7, I8). However, the paper does not present any between-group contrasts comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls (or bvFTD-only vs controls) in MNI/Talairach space; all reported results are within-group voxelwise regression analyses relating occupational scores to rCMRglc. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Decision: EXCLUDED because it fails to provide the required between-group contrast (I6).

This is an empirical study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=13) and appropriate healthy controls (n=25). Imaging includes VBM (GM voxelwise analyses in MNI space) alongside TBSS DTI analyses. The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain group contrasts for bvFTD versus controls (TBSS and VBM results displayed on the MNI standard brain and described in text/figures), satisfying the requirement for defined stochastic space coordinates/standard space reporting. All required sample size and whole-brain reporting criteria are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review; not ROI-only; no disallowed modality-only report). Full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, References) is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the bvFTD-focused meta-analysis.

This is an empirical study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD (I4) with adequate group sizes (17 bvFTD, 22 controls; I5). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise comparisons of cortical measures between bvFTD and controls using SPM/standard stereotactic space and presents region results (I6, I7, I8). However, the imaging analysis is cortical thickness/volumetric MRI rather than VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET. The review exclusion criterion E9 explicitly excludes studies that report only cortical thickness methods. Also, inclusion criterion I3 (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) is not met. Therefore the study must be excluded.

Although the study used FDG-PET (meets I3), it does not provide a group-level, whole-brain between-group contrast specifically for behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD). The FTLD sample is pooled (FTD N=3, SD N=6, mixed N=4) and the paper presents comparisons of FTLD (pooled) and AD versus SCI controls rather than a separate bvFTD (FTD) versus control contrast. The number of bvFTD/FTD cases is only 3 (<6), so the bvFTD patient group does not meet the minimum sample size (I5). Therefore the study fails I4 (target sample not separably reported as bvFTD), I5 (bvFTD group <6), I6 (no bvFTD-vs-control whole-brain contrast where bvFTD are not pooled), and I7 (no whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD target group).

Study uses FDG-PET (I3 satisfied). However it does not provide data specific to clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease: the FTLD group includes 13 patients with only 3 labelled as 'FTD' (not specified as bvFTD), so there is no distinct bvFTD group (I4 not met). The bvFTD-relevant subgroup size is <6 (FTD n=3), so the sample-size criterion for the target group is not met (I5 not met). The reported between-group voxelwise contrasts are for aggregated FTLD (vs subjective cognitive impairment) rather than a bvFTD group unpooled from other diagnoses, so there is no between-group contrast specific to bvFTD (I6 not met) and no whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD sample (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (11) compared to 11 healthy controls. The study used whole-brain voxel-wise VBM (SPM5) including a two-sample t-test comparing bvFTD vs controls and reports group-level, whole-brain results (FDR-corrected maps presented; Figure 1) and voxelwise correlations with YBOCS. Sample sizes meet minimum thresholds. The manuscript includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets the review requirements for inclusion.

The study reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) whole-brain group analyses (coordinates in MNI space) comparing a genetically defined C9ORF72 mutation group (n=11) to healthy controls (n=15), and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases within the sample. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (bvFTD patients are included in the sample), I5 (patient group and control group sizes ≥6), I7 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), and I8 (results reported in standard space/figures). However, the meta-analysis requires contrasts that specifically compare a clinically defined bvFTD group (not pooled with other patient subtypes) to controls (I6). This paper’s between-group contrasts are for a genetic C9ORF72 group with mixed clinical syndromes (bvFTD, FTD–MND, PPA, etc.), not a bvFTD-only group, so I6 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met. Full text appears complete.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); includes clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD subjects (bvFTD) in separate genetic groups (I4); patient groups and controls meet the minimum sample-size threshold (each patient group ≥12 and controls n=40) (I5); reports group-level between-group voxelwise contrasts (VBM) comparing bvFTD groups to controls and between disease groups using SPM with whole-brain results (figures and voxelwise thresholds described) (I6); provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results clearly identified for the target groups (I7); and whole-brain results are presented in figures/tables in the text (I8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract provided). The abstract indicates use of voxel-based morphometry (I3) and inclusion of a bvFTD sample (I4). However, critical details required for inclusion are missing: sample sizes for patient and control groups (I5) are not reported; it is unclear whether results include between-group contrasts reported in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing bvFTD to controls without pooling (I6); and it is not confirmed that at least one whole-brain, group-level voxelwise result is reported for the target bvFTD group (I7). No exclusion criteria are met based on available information. Because the full text (methods and results with coordinates/tables) is not provided, I cannot verify all required inclusion criteria; therefore I exclude pending full text.

This study is excluded because, although it uses VBM (I3) and includes clinically-diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s patients (I4), it does not report a whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD group (not pooled with other FTD subtypes) to controls in stereotactic coordinates. Thus it fails I6 and I7. The bvFTD subgroup sample size for a standalone bvFTD vs control contrast is not reported clearly, so I5 is not confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

Although the study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (total n=252 across controls and three dementia syndromes), it does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrast that compares bvFTD patients alone to healthy controls. The reported whole-brain VBM results (with MNI coordinates) are for a Val allele dose linear contrast across all subjects (controls + AD + bvFTD + SemD) rather than a bvFTD vs control contrast where bvFTD is not pooled with other patient groups. Therefore the study fails to meet I6 (bvFTD-specific between-group contrast with coordinates) and I7 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD sample). I3 (VBM modality), I4 (includes bvFTD sample), and I5 (adequate sample size overall and implied per-group sizes) are satisfied. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were met.

Exclusion IDs met: E6 (study reports ROI/parcellation analyses without whole-brain voxelwise results) and E9 (reports surface-based cortical volumes/parcellation rather than qualifying modalities). Inclusion IDs met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients; n=32) and I5 (patient and control groups both ≥6 participants). Inclusion IDs NOT met: I3 (does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET; uses Freesurfer regional volumes), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrast reported in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD vs controls), and I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results). The full text is complete for screening. Because the imaging modality and whole-brain voxelwise reporting requirements are not satisfied, the study does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

This study meets the review objectives and reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) results comparing bvFTD patients to healthy controls. It includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (bvFTD groups reported) with group sizes >6 (bvFTD C9+ n=15; bvFTD noncarriers n=48) and healthy controls (recruited and used in VBM comparisons). Whole-brain, voxelwise VBM analyses are reported (interaction effects, pFWE≤0.05) with results referenced in figures and a coordinate table (table e-3), satisfying requirement for defined stochastic space reporting. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. One minor uncertainty is the explicit control group sample size not stated in the excerpt, but controls are clearly used in voxelwise analyses. Given these facts, the study should be included.

This is an empirical VBM study reporting whole-brain, voxelwise comparisons involving a clearly defined bvFTD group. The paper uses voxel-based morphometry (SPM5) (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=49) (I4) and an age-matched healthy control group (n=30) satisfying the minimum sample-size requirement (I5). The manuscript reports between-group whole-brain contrasts and voxelwise regression results, with peak coordinates converted to Talairach space (I6,I7,I8). The full text contains introduction, methods (neuropsychology and structural imaging), results (including tables/figures of atrophy and regressions), and discussion, and no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be included.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. It uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as an imaging modality and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons (TFCE, permutation testing) in MNI standard space. The sample includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=15) and a healthy control group (n=18), exceeding the minimum size threshold. The paper reports between-group contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls that are not pooled with other patient groups and presents whole-brain results in figures/overlays with MNI-based processing, satisfying I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8. No exclusion criteria apply. The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical VBM study (voxel-based morphometry) with accompanying whole-brain voxelwise analyses comparing clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients to healthy controls. The sample includes 13 bvFTD patients and 19 controls (both >6). Methods state images were normalized to MNI space and voxelwise two-sample t-tests were performed; Results explicitly include a section “Voxel-wise comparisons between bvFTD and CN” reporting whole-brain findings. The paper therefore meets modality (VBM), target sample (bvFTD), sample size, and whole-brain between-group contrast requirements. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; no exclusion criteria are met (not a review; not ROI-only; no disallowed comorbid sample; not DTI-only). Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it uses structural MRI morphometry (manual/automated segmentation and radial distance shape mapping of the putamen), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, and reports ROI-based shape/volume analyses rather than whole-brain voxelwise results with stereotactic coordinates. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E6 (reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD patients), I5 (sample sizes: FTD n=33, controls n=17). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is structural morphometry, not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach coordinate space), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported). Full text appears complete for assessment.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain voxelwise reporting requirements. Exclusion criterion met: E6 (reports ROI/volumetric analyses and no whole-brain voxelwise statistical results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (participants clinically diagnosed with bvFTD), I5 (patient group n≥6 and control group n≥6 for imaging). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (did not use VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET; study used structural MRI volumetry/FreeSurfer/BSI and fluid registration), I6 (no between-group contrast reported in MNI/Talairach space with coordinates), I7 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results identified for the target sample). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients meeting Neary/revised criteria (I4), reports adequate sample sizes (20 bvFTD, 18 controls) exceeding the minimum of 6 per group (I5), and presents between-group voxelwise contrasts with stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) comparing bvFTD to controls without pooling with other patient groups (I6). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results corrected for multiple comparisons and describes coordinates in tables/figures (I7,I8). No exclusion criteria are met: the study is empirical (not a review), includes whole-brain analyses (not ROI-only), excludes comorbid psychiatric/other dementias in its sample, and does not rely solely on seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. Therefore the paper should be included in the review.

Although this empirical study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=11) and healthy controls and uses [18F]-FDG-PET (I3, I4, I5), and reports voxel-based SPM results with coordinates (I8), it does not provide a voxelwise between-group contrast comparing the bvFTD group to controls in MNI/Talairach space. PET analyses were performed on patients only (AD and bvFTD combined in regression analyses) and reported correlations with deficit scores across patients, with no clear whole‑brain group-level bvFTD vs control contrast. Thus inclusion criteria I6 (between-group contrast bvFTD vs controls) and I7 (a whole‑brain group-level voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD group) are not met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical resting-state fMRI study of frontotemporal dementia that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (n=8) and healthy controls (n=16). Whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses (SPM) are reported, including between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs. controls and bvFTD vs. SD) with stereotactic coordinates provided (e.g., BA46 peak x=36,y=42,z=30) and cluster-level results. The paper reports behavioral correlations, correction for gray-matter atrophy, and whole-brain results in the main text and supplementary materials. All required inclusion criteria are met (I3: resting-state fMRI; I4: clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample; I5: patient and control group sizes ≥6; I6: between-group contrasts with stereotactic coordinates for bvFTD vs controls; I7: whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results from the target group; I8: results clearly described in text and supplementary data). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (>=6 patients and >=6 controls), I7 (reports group-level voxelwise (VBM) results from the patient group), I8 (neuroanatomical results summarized in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 — the study does not report a between-group whole-brain contrast comparing bvFTD patients to healthy controls in standard stereotactic space; the imaging analyses are within-patient VBM regressions (correlations with task performance) rather than patient-versus-control voxelwise comparisons. No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be satisfied and I6 is not met, the study is excluded.

Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study used voxel-based morphometry), I4 (included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, n=24), I5 (patient group size ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 and I7. The paper does not report any between-group VBM contrast comparing bvFTD to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space; imaging analyses are voxelwise whole-brain correlations of insight scores across a mixed patient cohort and follow-up within-group analyses produced no significant bvFTD-specific whole-brain results. Thus there are no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD group (I7), nor a bvFTD-versus-control between-group contrast (I6). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded for not meeting the critical between-group/target-group whole-brain reporting requirements (I6, I7).

This VBM study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) using VBM imaging (I3) with >=6 patients (n=20) (I5). However, it does not report any between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls (no bvFTD vs control results), so inclusion criteria I6 is not met. Analyses are voxelwise but were restricted to a frontal mask rather than reporting whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results, so I7 (whole-brain evidence) is not met. Therefore it fails required inclusion criteria. Exclusion criterion E6 applies because the paper provides masked/region-restricted voxelwise analyses without whole-brain results. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This original empirical study reports resting-state fMRI (and VBM) in clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (12 bvFTD) with healthy controls (30) and pAD (18). It provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise comparisons (SPM8 analyses, results reported at p<.05 FWE cluster-level) in MNI space, including contrasts of bvFTD versus controls and bvFTD versus pAD. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review article, ROI-only, seed-based-only, comorbid psychiatric/substance samples) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

This study uses VBM and includes adequate sample sizes (FTD n=37, controls present), but does not clearly meet key inclusion criteria for this bvFTD-focused review. Specifically, the FTD sample is not clearly described as clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (only 4/37 explicitly described as behavioural variant), so I4 is not satisfied. The full text does not report any between-group voxelwise contrast coordinates in a defined stereotactic space (MNI or Talairach), nor does it present clearly a group-level whole-brain voxelwise result in stereotactic coordinates; therefore I6 and I7 are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used) and I5 (sample sizes >=6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I6, I7. Consequently the study is excluded.

This study is excluded because the VBM analyses were constrained to a fronto-striatal ROI mask (region-of-interest voxelwise analysis) rather than reporting whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results. Thus it meets exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (bvFTD sample clinically diagnosed, n=11), I5 (bvFTD n>=6 and controls n>=6), I6 (between-group contrasts reported in stereotactic space comparing bvFTD to controls). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (does not report at least one whole-brain, voxelwise group-level result for the target sample; analyses were ROI-restricted). Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper must be excluded from the meta-analysis because it provides only ROI-limited voxelwise findings rather than qualifying whole-brain results required by the review.

The study uses VBM (satisfies I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (bvFTD n=17; satisfies I4), and meets the minimum sample-size requirement (bvFTD n=17, controls n=18; satisfies I5). However, all reported voxelwise whole-brain VBM analyses are presented for the pooled FTD group (n=52) rather than for the bvFTD subgroup alone, and the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain between-group contrasts or coordinate tables specifically comparing bvFTD to controls. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (bvFTD-specific whole-brain results/contrasts in standard space) are not met. No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered. The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this study used VBM and FDG-PET and reports whole-brain voxelwise group analyses, it is excluded because it does not provide bvFTD-specific between-group contrasts. The FTLD patient sample (n=11) is a mixed group (FTD n=4, semantic dementia n=5, mixed n=2) and results are reported for the pooled FTLD group versus controls rather than for a clinically defined bvFTD (behavioral-variant FTD) subgroup. Therefore: (a) I6 is not satisfied (no between-group contrast specifically for bvFTD vs. controls in stereotactic coordinates); (b) I4 is not satisfied (bvFTD diagnosis is not clearly isolated/present as a target sample); (c) I5 is not satisfied for a bvFTD subgroup because the FTD subgroup has only 4 patients (<6). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3 (VBM/FDG-PET used), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I8 (results clearly described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) applied. Full text appears complete.

This study uses FDG-PET and includes >6 FTD patients overall, but it does not specifically report clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease as a clearly identified target group (I4 not met). The paper reports multivariate classification/discriminative images after MNI normalization, but it does not provide an explicit between-group voxelwise contrast (with coordinates) that compares a bvFTD group to controls in MNI/Talairach space (I6 not met). It is therefore not possible to confirm that a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise result from a bvFTD-only sample is reported (I7 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET modality) and I5 (sample sizes >=6 across groups). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because key inclusion criteria I4, I6, and I7 are not satisfied.

This is an empirical study that used task-based BOLD fMRI and voxel-based morphometric (VBM) volumetric MRI analyses comparing bvFTD patients to healthy controls. The sample includes 16 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and 16 healthy seniors (both ≥6). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts (bvFTD vs. controls) using SPM8 with FDR-corrected thresholds and cluster extent, and presents overlapping ROIs and coordinates (reported in figures/tables) in a standard stereotactic space. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

The full text reports empirical neuroimaging data in a clinically diagnosed bvFTD cohort using voxel-based morphometry and task-based fMRI (satisfies I3). The sample includes >6 bvFTD patients (10 behavioral analyses, 8 in neuroimaging) and 16 controls (satisfies I4 and I5). The paper reports between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (VBM and fMRI) comparing bvFTD patients to controls, with results presented in tables/figures and coordinates (satisfies I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply: this is not a review/meta-analysis, includes whole-brain analyses (not ROI-only), and does not report only seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness; there is no indication of comorbid psychiatric diagnoses or other dementia pooling that would violate E7. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical VBM study that directly investigates bvFTD. It uses whole-brain VBM (FSL–VBM) and reports voxelwise, group-level contrasts and correlations in MNI space. The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=10) and healthy controls (n=10), meeting sample size thresholds. The paper presents whole-brain voxelwise results comparing bvFTD to controls (and bvFTD vs AD), with anatomical labels and coordinates, and describes permutation-based nonparametric testing. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion, so the record is complete.

This is an empirical, whole-brain VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=19) and healthy controls (n=19). The study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality and reports voxelwise, whole-brain group contrasts and brain-behavior correlations with anatomical coordinates referenced to MNI space (tables/figures and MNI coordinates are described). The bvFTD group is analyzed separately (bvFTD vs Controls) and not pooled with other patient groups. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, no major comorbidities reported, not a non-empirical paper, and not limited to seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8.

This study used FDG-PET (I3 satisfied) and included an FTLD patient group of n=11 (I5 satisfied). However it does not report clinically labeled bvFTD/Pick’s disease explicitly (I4 not clearly met), and crucially it does not provide whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing bvFTD to healthy controls; results are reported as regional/ROI hypometabolism counts and pattern descriptions rather than voxelwise coordinates (I6 and I7 not met). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI/regional analyses without whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Exclusion applied: E6 (study reports ROI-based network/graph analyses using AAL parcellation and inter-regional correlations but does not present voxelwise, whole-brain group-level contrasts in standard stereotactic space). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (resting-state fMRI used), I4 (sample = clinically probable bvFTD patients), I5 (>=6 patients and controls). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 and I7 (no reported between-group voxelwise results in MNI/Talairach space and no whole-brain voxelwise group-level coordinates reported). Full text appears complete and methods/results are detailed, but the analytic approach is region-of-interest/parcellation-based rather than voxelwise whole-brain coordinate-based, so it fails the review’s requirement for voxelwise whole-brain results.

This is an empirical study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (SPM8) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons and voxelwise correlations. The sample includes 18 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and 18 healthy controls (and 21 PSP patients), meeting the minimum sample-size requirement. The paper reports separate between-group contrasts (controls > FTD and controls > PSP), and voxelwise results clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD group; results are presented in standard normalized template space (SPM/VBM pipeline). No exclusion criteria are met: this is not a review/meta-analysis, it includes whole-brain analyses (not only ROI), excludes concurrent psychiatric disorders per methods, and does not use only seed-based FC/DTI/cortical-thickness methods. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; full text appears complete. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within FTLD sample), I5 (patient group N=37, >6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group contrast reported comparing a bvFTD group versus healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space—the VBM contrasts compare musicophilic vs non-musicophilic FTLD subgroups, not bvFTD vs controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD-only target sample). Exclusion criteria: none met. Therefore exclude because the study does not provide the required bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain between-group contrasts (I6/I7).

This is an empirical VBM study in PLOS ONE that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=18) and healthy controls (n=27). It uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality and reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs controls) with MNI stereotaxic coordinates and figures; analyses were performed separately for bvFTD (not pooled with other FTD subtypes). The study also provides group-level whole-brain results (FWE-corrected atrophy maps and uncorrected voxelwise correlations reported with cluster extent) and presents coordinates in text/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., review/meta-analysis, ROI-only, DTI/FC-only methods, or samples with disqualifying comorbidities) are violated. Full text appears complete.

This is a methods/design paper describing an ongoing cohort (LOF study) and does not report empirical whole-brain voxelwise comparisons or coordinate results for clinically diagnosed bvFTD versus controls. Exclusion criteria met: E8 (non-empirical/methods-only paper without original voxelwise imaging results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET is included as an imaging modality in the study design) and I5 (sample size exceeds 6 participants — cohort includes ~130 patients). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (participants are a symptom-based LOF cohort, not a sample of clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s disease patients), I6 (no reported between-group contrasts in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls), and I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results are reported). Full text appears complete (contains background, methods, and discussion), but lacks the required empirical imaging results for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This full-text reports an empirical voxel-based morphometry (VBM) study (FSL VBM) examining dementia groups including a clearly defined behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD) subgroup (n=11). Controls (n=15) meet the control sample size requirement. The manuscript describes voxel-wise, whole-brain t-tests comparing each patient group (behavioural-variant FTD, semantic dementia, PNFA, Alzheimer’s disease) to controls, reports results overlaid on the MNI standard brain and provides cluster coordinates (voxelwise MNI space). Analyses specifically examine bvFTD (patterns of atrophy and correlations in bvFTD combined with controls), and results are presented as whole-brain voxelwise findings (figures/tables/supplementary). Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study used DTI tractography and a targeted VBM approach applied to an anterior cingulate mask rather than reporting whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons in stereotactic space with coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM method—FSL-VBM modification applied), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (≥6 patients and ≥6 controls). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no reported between-group contrast results in defined stereotactic space with coordinates/MNI or Talairach reported), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results—analyses were ROI/masked to the ACC and tract-specific). Exclusion criteria applied: E6 (study reports only ROI/tract-based analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore excluded for failing whole-brain/voxelwise reporting requirements.

The study uses resting-state fMRI (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (5 of 15) with a patient group >=6 and control group >=6 (I4, I5). However, the paper’s voxelwise whole-brain between-group comparison was performed on the pooled FTD sample (bvFTD + semantic dementia) versus controls to define ROIs; the manuscript does not report a whole-brain, voxelwise contrast specifically comparing the bvFTD group to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore it fails to meet I6 (between-group contrast for bvFTD vs controls) and I7 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise result coming from the target sample group). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are applicable. Full text appears complete.

This is a VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=12) and adequate control groups, and reports VBM analyses normalized to MNI space. However, the paper does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast that is clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD group vs controls. The bvFTD-versus-control results described are ROI-based / small-volume-corrected regional analyses rather than whole-brain voxelwise results specific to the bvFTD sample. Although a whole-brain contrast is reported for the pooled FTD group versus controls, the meta-analysis inclusion rules require whole-brain, target-sample-specific (bvFTD) voxelwise results. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met, so the study must be excluded.

The study uses resting-state fMRI and VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=19) and matched controls (n=19) meeting sample-size requirements (I4,I5). It reports voxel-wise, group-level whole-brain comparisons in standard space (MNI) using FSL randomize and provides MNI coordinates and figures (I6,I7,I8). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

Full text is complete. This fMRI resting-state study includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients (including 18 bvFTD cases) and reports whole-brain voxelwise ICA results correlating Reserve Index with functional connectivity. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (resting-state fMRI), I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases), I5 (patient subgroup size ≥6), I8 (results reported with MNI coordinates/voxelwise clusters). However, it does NOT meet I6: the paper does not report any between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls (bvFTD results are not presented as a distinct between-group contrast against controls). Consequently I7 is not met for the target comparison: there are no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD vs control contrast. Because both I6 and I7 are required, the study must be excluded.

The study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain reporting requirements. It uses diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) with an ROI approach (not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), and reports ROI-based results rather than whole-brain voxelwise coordinates/analyses in standardized space. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients) and I5 (bvFTD n=8 and controls n=12). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (required imaging modality VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET), I6 and I7 (required at least one between-group contrast reported in defined stochastic space and at least one whole-brain voxelwise group-level result). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) and E9 (DTI-only study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper must be excluded from this review.

This is an empirical study that includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and uses both VBM and task-based fMRI, with patient and control group sizes >6. However, the imaging group-level voxelwise contrasts reported are comparisons between AD and bvFTD (VBM) rather than between bvFTD and healthy controls. The paper does not present a whole-brain (voxelwise) group contrast explicitly comparing bvFTD to controls in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 (between-group contrast of bvFTD vs controls) and I7 (at least one group-level whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD vs control comparison). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM/fMRI used), I4 (bvFTD sample), I5 (sample sizes ≥6). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete. Given the missing required between-group whole-brain contrast comparing bvFTD to controls, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

Excluded because the study does not provide whole-brain, voxelwise results specific to a bvFTD group (bvFTD subgroup = 5 subjects). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (bvFTD patients were included in the sample), I5 (overall patient group n=15 and control group n=12 meet the >=6 requirement), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures/supplement). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group contrast reported that compares a bvFTD-only group to controls where bvFTD is not pooled with other FTD subtypes) and I7 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD-only target sample). No exclusion criteria were triggered (none of E5–E9 apply). Because the meta-analysis objective targets bvFTD-specific whole-brain contrasts (unpooled bvFTD group) and this study only reports mixed-FTD contrasts or subgroup analyses where the bvFTD cell has n<6, it does not meet all required inclusion criteria for this review.

Although this study uses whole-brain VBM in MNI space and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=18) with adequate control numbers, the provided full text does not report any between-group voxelwise contrast directly comparing the bvFTD group to healthy controls in standard space. It does report within-group whole-brain VBM covariate results for bvFTD (VBM correlations with IGT scores) but no explicit bvFTD vs. control voxelwise contrast coordinates/results are presented in the supplied text. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (at least one between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls) is not satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I7, I8. No exclusion criteria were triggered.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s required target diagnosis. Although it uses FDG-PET (I3) and appears to have sufficient group sizes (I5), the patient sample is described as heterogeneous FTLD (frontotemporal lobar degeneration) without specification that participants were clinically diagnosed with behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease. Therefore inclusion criterion I4 is not met. Consequently, the paper does not report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts specifically comparing a bvFTD (or Pick’s disease) group to controls (I6 and I7 are not satisfied for the target sample). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were triggered by the full text. Summary: exclusion IDs met: none; inclusion IDs met: I3, I5; inclusion IDs not met: I4, I6, I7. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical VBM study of bvFTD cases (both C9ORF72 carriers and sporadic bvFTD) including healthy controls. It reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (patient groups vs Controls) using MNI space and provides coordinates/figures (including supplementary table). Sample sizes meet the minimum (C9 n=8, sporadic bvFTD n=15, Controls n=15). Whole-brain group-level results for the target bvFTD groups are clearly identified. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and imaging details; therefore judged complete.

Meets all inclusion criteria for the review: (I3) uses VBM; (I4) includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=16); (I5) sample sizes meet thresholds (bvFTD=16, controls=18); (I6) reports between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI space (controls>FTD, FTD>PSP, etc.) where bvFTD is not pooled; (I7) provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise VBM results; (I8) whole-brain results are described in text/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, empirical data, no comorbid psychiatric/neuro disorders reported). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion E6 applied: the study reports only region-based visual MRI ratings and qualitative FDG-PET descriptions rather than any whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses with coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET used), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (≥6 patients and ≥6 controls). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no between-group contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results from target sample). Study meets multiple inclusion criteria (I3: uses VBM; I4: includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients; I5: adequate sample sizes; I6: reports between-group contrasts with MNI coordinates; I8: coordinates/figures reported). However, it does NOT provide whole-brain (voxelwise) results: the VBM analyses were explicitly limited/masked to frontal and temporal lobes, so no true whole-brain group-level voxelwise results are reported (I7 not met). This falls under exclusion criterion E6 (reports only ROI/masked analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Therefore, exclude.

This is an original empirical study including 27 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (meets I4) and 20 healthy controls (meets I5). The paper reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses in addition to DTI, satisfying the imaging-modality requirement (I3). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise comparisons are performed and results are projected to MNI space (meets I6 and I7), with results presented in figures/tables (I8). The bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled) and compared to controls and AD. No exclusion criteria apply: this is not a review (E5), includes whole-brain results (not only ROI, so not E6), is empirical (not E8), and although it includes DTI, it also includes VBM (so E9 does not apply). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This full text reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses (FSL-VBM) and provides group-level, voxelwise contrasts comparing patient groups to healthy controls with MNI coordinates and figures/tables. The sample includes clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD) patients (n=10) and healthy controls (n=14), meeting the minimum N≥6 requirement. The paper reports between-group VBM contrasts for bvFTD versus controls and covariate analyses (age, comprehension) with whole-brain results clearly attributed to the bvFTD group. Imaging modality, sample, sample size, voxelwise whole-brain reporting, and coordinate reporting criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7,I8) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review; not ROI-only; no disqualifying comorbidities reported; empirical study; not solely FC/DTI/cortical thickness). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the bvFTD imaging meta-analysis. It includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=22) and healthy controls (n=34), both >6 participants. The paper performed voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) with scans registered to MNI152 space and voxelwise whole-brain analyses (I7), reporting patient–control group comparisons (bvFTD vs. controls) that replicated the visual-rating findings; these results are referenced in the main text and in supplementary figures (I8). The VBM contrasts were conducted in standard space (MNI) and involve between-group contrasts where bvFTD is not pooled with other patient groups (I6). Sample sizes satisfy I5 and clinical diagnosis criteria satisfy I4. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary figures are externally linked but acceptable, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study uses FDG-PET (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) with >6 patients in the bvFTD group (15; I5). However, it does not report any between-group voxelwise contrasts in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing the bvFTD group to controls, nor does it present group-level whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinate tables/figures suitable for meta-analysis. Instead it reports diagnostic categorizations (positive/normal/non-FTD) and sensitivity/specificity, without voxelwise statistical maps or coordinates. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Exclusion criteria: none met.

Although the study uses VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=28) (I4), and meets sample-size requirements for patients and controls (I5), it does not present any between-group voxelwise contrast comparing the bvFTD group directly to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space (I6 not met). The VBM results are regression-based across a pooled, mixed-diagnosis sample (polisher/neutral and tarnisher/neutral analyses) and do not report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results coming specifically from the bvFTD subgroup (I7 not met). Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. Although it includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=11) and reports whole-brain voxel-wise TBM results (including voxel-wise regressions within the bvFTD group), the imaging modality used is tensor-based morphometry (TBM), not one of the required modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) (I3 not met). In addition, the primary between-group contrasts reported compare bvFTD to early-onset Alzheimer’s disease (AD), not to healthy control subjects as required by the criterion specifying a between-group contrast versus controls in standard stereotaxic space (I6 not met).
