This empirical study meets the review objectives and all inclusion criteria. It uses resting-state fMRI and voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (12 patients) with matched healthy controls (I4,I5), reports group-level between-group contrasts and analyses in standard stereotaxic/MNI space (SPM normalization and voxelwise VBM results) (I6), and presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (thresholded and FDR-corrected) described in the text and supplementary materials (I7,I8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete for screening purposes.

Exclusion criteria met: E6 and E9. This study reports ROI-based analyses (FreeSurfer cortical/WM ROIs and JHU DTI ROIs) and DTI/cortical-volume measures rather than voxelwise, whole-brain (voxelwise) results in standardized stereotactic space. It does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET as the primary imaging modality. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample, n=14) and I5 (patient group size >=6; AD comparison group n=19). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (study does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET as required), I6 (no between-group contrast reported in MNI/Talairach coordinate space), and I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore, exclude per E6 (only ROI analyses/no whole-brain results) and E9 (only DTI/cortical-volume methods rather than required modalities).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: I3 (uses voxel-based morphometry/voxel-wise gray matter analyses and ICA on T1-weighted MRI), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients diagnosed per Rascovsky criteria with multidisciplinary consensus and CSF measures), I5 (sample sizes exceed minimum: 24 bvFTD, 31 AD, 30 controls), I6 (reports between-group contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls using voxelwise analyses in MNI space and SCN maps), I7 (provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results — TFCE, FWE-corrected VBM results and whole-brain SCN analyses), and I8 (results are presented and described in figures/tables/text). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, not solely seed-based FC/DTI/thickness). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore include for the review of bvFTD imaging studies.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group and reports whole-brain voxelwise group comparisons. Methods describe VBM preprocessing normalized to MNI space and whole-brain analyses; results include bvFTD vs. control voxelwise atrophy patterns and direct patient-group contrasts. Sample sizes meet the minimum (23 bvFTD patients; 50 controls). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only, non-VBM modality, comorbid psychiatric/other-dementia sample, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study satisfies all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is a genetic/clinical case series of TBK1 mutation carriers that includes several patients with behavioural-variant FTD and used FDG-PET in two patients (so I3, I4, and I5 are met: FDG-PET modality present; study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients; there are ≥6 FTD patients in the cohort). However, the paper does not report any group-level between-group voxelwise contrasts in a standard stereotaxic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls, nor any whole-brain, voxelwise group results or coordinate tables/figures suitable for meta-analysis. Therefore it fails I6 and I7. Because no whole-brain group results are provided, it falls under the exclusion of studies without whole-brain results (E6). Full text appears complete.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry and includes a clinical bvFTD sample (n=24) with healthy controls (n=24), and reports whole-brain voxelwise VBM findings for the bvFTD group. However, the VBM analyses described are within-group voxelwise correlations (neuroanatomical associations with language performance in the bvFTD group) rather than a between-group voxelwise contrast directly comparing bvFTD versus controls in stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) space. Inclusion criterion I6 (at least one between-group contrast comparing bvFTD group to controls) is not met. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore the paper must be excluded under the review rules.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=12) and healthy controls (n=12). The authors performed whole-brain, voxel-wise VBM analyses (TFCE, FWE-corrected) and report group-level between-group contrasts and anatomical coordinates in MNI space. Sample sizes meet the ≥6 requirement for patient and control groups. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (including imaging and VBM pipeline), Results (neuroimaging group contrasts and tables), and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, no disqualifying comorbidities reported, and not limited to FC/DTI/cortical thickness). Therefore the study satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and should be included.

This empirical study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) normalized to MNI space and reports between-group (bvFTD vs. controls) voxelwise contrasts with cluster-level FWE correction (I3, I6, I7, I8). The sample comprises clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=26) and matched healthy controls (n=23), satisfying diagnostic and sample-size requirements (I4, I5). The full text includes Introduction, Methods (behavioral and MRI/VBM), Results (behavioral and VBM), and Discussion; core article content is present (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria are met: it is not a review/meta-analysis (E5), does not report only ROI analyses (E6), is empirical with original data (not E8), and does not rely solely on excluded imaging modalities (E9); participant selection excluded other neurological/psychiatric disorders (E7 not applicable). Therefore, INCLUDE.

The study is excluded because it reports only ROI/parcellation-based metabolic connectivity analyses (60 AAL VOIs) and does not present any whole-brain, voxelwise, coordinate-based (MNI/Talairach) between-group contrasts for behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) versus controls. The FTLD group is analyzed as a pooled group including behavioral and language variants, and bvFTD-specific results are not reported separately. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET imaging), I4 (includes behavioral-variant FTLD patients within the sample), I5 (sample sizes meet minimums). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group, coordinate-based voxelwise contrasts reported comparing bvFTD separately to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (study reports only ROI/parcellation-based analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical study that used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (FSL-VBM) and reports voxelwise results with MNI coordinates. It includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=19) and healthy controls (n=25), meeting sample-size thresholds. The paper describes whole-brain, group-level t-tests comparing patient groups (including bvFTD) to controls and reports VBM covariate analyses (MNI coordinates) linked to eating behavior and sucrose preference. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, no disqualifying comorbid sample, and not limited to seed‑based FC/DTI/cortical thickness). The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text appears complete. Thus the study satisfies the required inclusion criteria for the review.

The study used VBM and resting-state fMRI (I3) and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (7 bvFTD cases within the FTD-GRN+ group) (I4). Sample sizes meet minimums (14 patients, control groups ≥6) (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group results (VBM and functional maps) (I7) and presents results in figures/tables (I8). However, the critical requirement I6 is not met: the reported between-group contrasts compare a combined FTD-GRN+ group (mixing bvFTD and avPPA) to controls rather than reporting a bvFTD-only versus control whole-brain contrast. The bvFTD subgroup is pooled with other FTD phenotypes in the main analyses, so no bvFTD-specific whole-brain contrast is available. No exclusion criteria were triggered. Therefore the study is excluded for failing inclusion criterion I6.

This is an original empirical neuroimaging study of clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (Rascovsky criteria). It used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on MRI and FDG-PET with voxelwise SPM5 analyses and partial-volume correction, reporting group-level whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (patients vs. controls) with tables/figures in stereotactic space. Sample size is 15 bvFTD patients and 15 matched healthy controls (>=6 each). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria were met (not a review, not ROI-only, no comorbid psychiatric/substance cases, not non-empirical, and not only seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness). Therefore the paper meets all required inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical resting-state fMRI study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD (I3, I4) with adequate sample sizes (14 bvFTD, 12 controls) meeting I5. However, the paper performs ROI-based graph-theory analyses (AAL parcellation, Network Centrality averaged across ROIs) and reports network-level differences rather than voxelwise, whole-brain coordinate results in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). Therefore it does not meet I6 and I7 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach) and qualifies for exclusion under E6 (reports only ROI/network analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7. Exclusion criteria applied: E6.

This study used VBM (I3), included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=13, I4), and had adequate sample sizes for patients and controls (bvFTD n=13; controls n=20, I5). However, the VBM analyses reported are correlational within a combined patient cohort and significant effects were reported only within pre-specified regions of interest; no between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD versus controls in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) are presented, and no whole-brain group-level voxelwise results for the bvFTD group are reported. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. This meets exclusion criterion E6 (reports only ROI findings / no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=33) with healthy controls (n=34). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise two-sample t-tests were performed in MNI space with results reported (figures and supplementary tables of coordinates) for bvFTD versus controls; cerebellar analyses used SUIT but whole-brain VBM results for the cerebral cortex are presented. The bvFTD group was not pooled with other patient groups in the reported between-group contrasts. Sample sizes exceed the minimum. Therefore all required inclusion criteria for VBM studies of bvFTD are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clearly defined bvFTD patient group (n=22) and age-matched controls (n=38). The paper uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and reports voxelwise, whole-brain (voxelwise GLM with permutation testing) group contrasts between bvFTD and controls with MNI coordinates and cluster thresholds provided (I6, I7). Sample sizes meet the minimum (I5). The bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled) and the paper provides group-level whole-brain results in the main text and supplementary tables/figures (I4, I8). Full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and tables/figures descriptions, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and should be INCLUDED.

This empirical study reports voxelwise, whole-brain SPM analyses of both 18F-FDG PET and voxel-based morphometry (GM density) comparing a bvFTD patient group to healthy controls. It used SPM8 with customized templates, reports Talairach-corrected coordinates and cluster-level inference, and presents group-level between-group contrasts for the whole bvFTD sample and bvFTD subgroups (bvFTD+ and bvFTD−) vs controls. Sample sizes meet thresholds (25 patients, 20 controls). The bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, no disallowed imaging-only methods, and no comorbid psychiatric/other dementia confounds). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8.

The study reports VBM and DTI analyses in clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and controls with MNI coordinates provided (I3, I4, I5, I6 satisfied). However, the imaging analyses were conducted using an ROI mask confined to predefined motor-system regions rather than reporting whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results. Therefore it does not provide whole-brain voxelwise results from the target sample (I7 not met) and meets exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the key disease-sample and contrast requirements for inclusion. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (voxel-based morphometry was used) and I5 (patient groups, e.g., FTLD n=55, exceed the minimum of 6 participants). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the sample does not report a clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease group specifically — participants are classified by pathological FTLD subtypes rather than a bvFTD clinical subgroup), I6 (no between-group contrast is reported specifically comparing a bvFTD group to controls in MNI/Talairach space — reported contrasts are for FTLD/FTLD subgroups, not bvFTD), and I7 (there is no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD target sample). Exclusion criteria met: none (no applicable exclusion criteria such as review-only, ROI-only, DTI/FC-only, comorbid sample, or non-empirical). Full text appears complete. Because the review requires results specifically for clinically defined bvFTD (or Pick’s) groups and voxelwise between-group contrasts for that group, this paper cannot be included.

Full text reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses: images normalized to MNI space and whole-brain voxel-wise comparisons were performed. Sample includes 18 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (per diagnostic criteria) and 18 healthy controls (both >6). The paper reports between-group whole-brain contrasts (bvFTD vs controls) and regression analyses relating atrophy to behavior, with results presented in figures/tables. This meets imaging modality (I3), bvFTD sample (I4), sample size (I5), between-group MNI-space contrasts (I6), whole-brain group-level voxelwise results (I7), and acceptable reporting formats (I8). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; not ROI-only; no prohibited modalities; no disqualifying comorbidities reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

Excluded because the study used atlas-based ROI volumetry on T1-weighted MRI (no VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) and reports only region-of-interest volumetric comparisons without any whole-brain voxelwise (MNI/Talairach) coordinates or group-level voxelwise contrasts comparing a bvFTD group to controls. Exclusion criterion met: E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants) and I5 (patient groups and control group sizes meet the ≥6 threshold). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group contrast reported in a defined stochastic space for bvFTD vs controls), and I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results). Full text appears complete.

Exclusion applied: E9 (study reports only cortical thickness methods). Inclusion met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample included), I5 (sufficient sample sizes: 37 bvFTD, 33 controls), I7 (whole-brain vertex-wise cortical thickness analyses performed), I8 (results reported with supplementary material). Inclusion not met: I3 (required imaging modality VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET — this study used structural MRI cortical thickness and subcortical volumetry via FreeSurfer), I6 (unclear/no between-group results reported in a defined stereotactic coordinate space such as MNI/Talairach; vertex-wise surface results do not provide standard voxel coordinates in the paper text). The full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded because it uses cortical thickness methods (excluded by E9) and does not meet the required imaging modalities (I3).

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=84) and uses whole-brain VBM (I3, I4, I5 satisfied) and reports voxelwise results/coordinates (I8 satisfied), it does not report any between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls (no control group or bvFTD-vs-control voxelwise contrast). Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 (bvFTD vs controls contrast) and I7 (whole-brain voxelwise result originating from the bvFTD vs control comparison). Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clearly defined bvFTD subgroup (n=64) and compares clinical phenotypes (including bvFTD) to healthy controls (n=32) using whole-brain voxelwise analyses. Imaging modality is VBM (I3). The sample contains clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) and the bvFTD group and controls exceed the 6-participant minimum (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results for each phenotype vs controls and specifies statistical thresholds and cluster reporting; results for bvFTD vs controls are described and illustrated (I6, I7). The manuscript references figures and supplementary material for spatial results (acceptable per I8). No exclusion criteria apply. Although coordinate tables are not embedded in the provided excerpt, the methods and references to figures/supplementary materials indicate voxelwise results in a standard space; thus the study meets inclusion criteria for this review.

This is a VBM study that includes bvFTD patients (7/10 in the SQSTM1 carrier group), uses whole-brain VBM, and has adequate group sizes; however, the reported whole-brain voxelwise contrasts are for the mixed FTD/SQSTM1 carrier group (which includes bvFTD and other FTD subtypes) rather than a bvFTD-only group. The review requires at least one between-group whole-brain contrast clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD group that is not pooled with other patient groups (I6, I7). Because the study does not report bvFTD-specific whole-brain contrasts, it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 and must be excluded.

This study is excluded because it reports only ROI-based structural MRI and ASL perfusion analyses rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET voxelwise whole-brain analyses. Exclusion ID met: E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion IDs met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients) and I5 (patient group N=11 and control group N=20, both ≥6). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (does not report between-group contrasts in standard coordinate space [MNI/Talairach] for voxelwise results), and I7 (does not report group-level whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Given these mismatches with the imaging and whole-brain reporting criteria, the study does not meet all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=15) (I4) and healthy controls (n=20) with adequate sample sizes (>6) (I5). The paper reports between-group VBM contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls and provides whole-brain voxelwise results in MNI space, including tables/figures of atrophy patterns and coordinates (I6, I7, I8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria are met (no review/meta-analysis only, not ROI-only, not seed-based FC/DTI/cortical-thickness only, and sample comorbidities are exclusionary criteria but are not present).

The study is excluded because it does not use the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) required by I3, and it does not report between-group coordinates in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) required by I6. It does include clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=9) and controls (n=18) satisfying I4 and I5, and it reports whole-brain voxelwise DTI (TBSS) results (I7). However, the meta-analysis requires specific modalities (I3), which are absent (study uses DTI, ASL perfusion, and structural ROI volumetry), and no between-group coordinate-based contrasts for bvFTD vs controls are provided (I6 not met). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical study that used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) whole-brain analyses to examine neural correlates of empathy in clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients. The sample includes 24 bvFTD patients and 22 healthy controls (both >6). The paper reports voxel-wise, whole-brain between-group contrasts and covariate analyses with anatomical results reported in MNI stereotaxic space (coordinates and tables/figures referenced). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review article, ROI-only analysis, excluded comorbid samples, non-empirical methods) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis focused on bvFTD VBM studies.

This is an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (23 patients included) with a healthy control group (20 controls). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise VBM group comparisons (two-sample t-test) showing atrophic clusters in bilateral anterior temporal lobes and additional regions, and voxelwise regression analyses relating behavioral measures to GM volume in the patient group. Imaging modality includes VBM (and FDG-PET performed in most patients). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (patients=23, controls=20). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results comparing bvFTD to controls are reported. Full text contains Introduction, Methods (including VBM preprocessing and statistics), Results (behavior and imaging) and Discussion; core article content is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and the reporting allowance I8. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete.

The full text reports voxelwise whole-brain structural MRI analyses (gray matter probability images processed with ANTs and Randomise permutation-based voxelwise tests in MNI space), meeting the imaging-modality requirement (I3). The sample includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=54) and healthy controls (n=27), meeting I4 and I5. The paper reports between-group GM atrophy contrasts and whole-brain regression analyses comparing each patient group (including bvFTD) to controls in stereotactic space (MNI), satisfying I6 and I7; whole-brain results are described in text/tables/figures (I8). The full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical study with FDG-PET and MRI in a clinically characterized bvFTD cohort, but it does not report any voxelwise/whole-brain (MNI/Talairach) between-group coordinate results. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET used), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), I5 (patient group N=27 ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group contrast in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain/voxelwise results), I8 (no whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures in standard space). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were directly triggered. Therefore exclude because key whole-brain/voxelwise reporting requirements (I6–I8) are not satisfied.

This study meets the review objective and all relevant imaging and sample criteria: (I3) uses Voxel-Based Morphometry (SPM8 VBM) as the imaging modality; (I4) includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=104, with 90 included in VBM analyses); (I5) adequate sample sizes (bvFTD n≈90; controls n=44); (I6) reports between-group VBM contrasts comparing bvFTD subgroups and the bvFTD cohort to age-matched controls (voxelwise T-maps reported and described); (I7) provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (FWE-corrected whole-brain VBM maps); (I8) whole-brain results are presented in figures and described in text (supplementary material referenced). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplemental materials are acknowledged. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met. Therefore the paper is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of whole-brain imaging in bvFTD.

The full text reports resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) and diffusion MRI analyses; rs-fMRI (ICA/dual-regression of the DMN) satisfies imaging modality criterion (I3). The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=12) and controls (n=17), meeting I4 and I5 (both groups ≥6). The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (Randomise, one-way ANCOVA and post-hoc t-tests) for DMN connectivity and TBSS-based DTI metrics; results are reported as cluster-based whole-brain findings with reference to supplement tables (acceptable per I6 and I8). Whole-brain voxelwise evidence from the target bvFTD group is clearly presented (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: this is an empirical study (not a review), reports whole-brain analyses (not ROI-only), and does not ONLY report seed-based FC, DTI, or cortical thickness (it includes whole-brain rs-fMRI ICA results). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This study reports VBM analyses and provides MNI coordinates relating gray matter atrophy to behavioral measures in bvFTD and AD, and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=39) and controls (n=61). However, the VBM analyses were constrained to an a priori ROI mask (Papez circuit and prefrontal regions) rather than reporting whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results. The paper therefore appears to present ROI-limited voxelwise results only and does not provide an unrestricted whole-brain voxelwise contrast for the bvFTD group vs. controls. According to the review criteria, whole-brain evidence is required; because only ROI-restricted analyses are reported, this meets exclusion criterion E6. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I6. Inclusion criterion not met: I7. Exclusion criterion met: E6.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses FDG-PET imaging (I3); includes clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (Rascovsky criteria) (I4) with N=52 (I5); reports voxelwise, whole-brain SPM analyses including a two-sample t-test comparing the bvFTD group (and subgroups) to a normal image database (n=112), i.e., between-group contrasts in stereotactic space (I6, I7). Whole-brain voxelwise results are described (and likely presented as SPM maps/figures), satisfying the acceptable reporting formats (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not a review, not ROI-only, not seed-based FC/DTI/cortical-thickness-only, and sample exclusions do not apply). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports empirical imaging and behavioral data on clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=14) and age-matched controls (n=19). It includes voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses and resting-state fMRI connectivity, reports whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts and coordinates (e.g., ATL [-45,13,-37]; IFG [-52,2,14]) in standard space, and provides group-level results comparing bvFTD to controls. Sample sizes meet thresholds. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (reviews, ROI-only, comorbid psychiatric/other dementia confounds, non-empirical, or limited-to-seed-only methods) apply based on provided content.

This study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants and reports voxelwise longitudinal structural MRI analyses, but it analyzes bvFTD and svPPA combined as a single FTLD group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (voxelwise structural MRI/voxel-based morphometry–type analysis of gray-matter change), I4 (bvFTD patients included in sample), I5 (patient and control group sizes >6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group contrast reported that isolates bvFTD vs controls; bvFTD data are pooled with svPPA), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results are reported for the combined FTLD group, not clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD target group). No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This empirical study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality and reports whole-brain, voxelwise comparisons of bvFTD patients (two bvFTD subgroups) versus healthy controls. Participants meet clinical bvFTD criteria (revised criteria) and group sizes are sufficient (34 bvFTD patients; 30 controls). The manuscript describes whole-brain VBM contrasts (AbvFTD vs controls; DbvFTD vs controls; AbvFTD vs DbvFTD) with FDR-corrected results and refers to Supplementary Table/Figure for VBM findings (coordinate tables/figures reported). Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is complete and the study does include VBM (I3), clinically diagnosed bv-FTD participants (n=15) (I4), and adequate group sizes with controls (I5). However, it does NOT report any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrast that isolates the bvFTD group versus controls in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The VBM results presented compare a subgroup defined by poor melody scores to controls and report correlations across pooled patient groups; they do not provide a bvFTD-specific voxelwise contrast or coordinates. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because the paper lacks bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain voxelwise results in stereotactic space (I6 and I7 not satisfied).

This is an empirical, longitudinal resting-state fMRI study (also includes VBM) comparing clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=12) to controls (n=22). The paper reports voxel-wise, whole-brain group-level contrasts and longitudinal voxel-based analyses (permutation testing, FWE correction) with results presented in figures/tables, comparing bvFTD versus controls (bvFTD not pooled). Whole-brain network-to-region and VBM results are described, satisfying requirements for stereotactic reporting and acceptable presentation formats. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only, irrelevant modalities, or disallowed comorbid samples) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The full text reports voxel-based morphometry and resting-state fMRI analyses (I3).
